fields.quoted_span:
The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the
Notice to Quit.
fields.note: D014 supports the core duties: notice at the same time as the Notice to Quit, a copy with Certificate of Compliance/Service to the Office of Housing Stability, non-waivability, FHE investigation, ISD enforcement, the warning then $300/day schedule, and that a violation does not halt eviction. It does not support the online portal, the tenant contact information submission, or the portal fine of up to $300/day; those come from D013, which is not in this document. The document names a mailing address, not a portal. Delivery with the notice of lease non-renewal or expiration is supported only in the tenant section.

fields.quoted_span:
1st Offense: Warning 
2nd and Subsequent Offenses: $300 per day
fields.note: The notice, the copy to the Office of Housing Stability, the penalty schedule, non-waivability and eviction not halted are all in D014. The portal non-submission fine up to $300/day is not in D014.

fields.quoted_span: The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.
The HSNA becomes effective on November 6, 2020.
fields.note: The document is framed as a current FAQ with the effective date given and no repeal or suspension. The in_force status is consistent with it.

fields.quoted_span:
The Ordinance applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners intending to end a
tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a unit in the City of Boston.
The only exempt properties are residences:
1. in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility;  and
2. in a non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term
treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance
abuse.
fields.note: The universal applicability and the two exemptions match the coverage summary. The absence of any size threshold is consistent with the document.

The document gives Sec. 10-11.7 in the enforcement table but not the 'Boston City Code' prefix. The aliases HSNA and Housing Stability Notification Act are supported. The chapter aliases 'ch. 10-11' and 'ch. 10' are not stated in the document.
